Friedrich Engels, The Condition of the Working Class in England, translated by Florence Kelley Wischnewetzky.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/friedrich-engels/the-condition-of-the-working-class-in-england/florence-kelley-wischnewetzky

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Friedrich Engels, the author, the annotator, the writer of the introduction and the writer of the preface, died 1895.
- Florence Kelley Wischnewetzky, the translator, died 1932.

First publication of the text used: 1885 (SE colophon: 'The Condition of the Working Class in England was published in 1845 by Friedrich Engels. It was translated from German in 1885 by Florence Kelley Wischnewetzky.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the Standard Ebooks rights statement says the text is in the US public domain, and the text was a translation first published in 1885, before 1931, so it is public domain there.
- Country of origin: the facts do not say in which country the text was first published. The possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India, South Africa and Germany. Each has a term of life + 70 years or less for these deaths, and the United States rule above applies there. The last to die did so in 1932, so the text is public domain in each of them by 1 January 2003.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
